Watch a panel of hilarious drag queens and nightlife celebrities, including Acid Betty, Ragamuffin, Merrie Cherry, Ruby Roo, roast master Misty Meaner and Bob the Drag Queen roast Brooklyn's own Thorgy Thor.

items.title: Lucy Balls
items.description: S1 E1 | Lucy Balls is a compelling artistic drag queen, but what about the person behind the makeup? In this episode, explore the duality of Lucy's life and see what makes her the captivating engaging queen the Brooklyn community has fallen in love with.

items.title: Untitled Queen
items.description: S1 E2 | Untitled Queen is more than just a polished Brooklyn drag performer. Behind the perfect makeup and intricate looks, is an art performance presented by an inspiring drag queen. Follow Untitled Queen on her journey as she proves to the world drag is an art form, and with her performances, one to be reckoned with.

items.title: Merrie Cherry
items.description: S1 E3 | Merrie Cherry and her larger than life personality are a staple in the Brooklyn drag scene. This confident drag queen grabs the bull by the horn and takes viewers along for the ride on her over the top drag journey and proves she has become a force to be reckoned with.

items.title: Hamm Samwich
items.description: S1 E4 | Hamm Samwich is an opinionated but loved enigma in the Brooklyn drag community. Through her performances and podcasts, Hamm expresses her unfiltered opinions and tells the stories of her life. In this episode, Hamm takes the world by storm and lets them know she's here to stay.

items.title: Misty Meaner & Mocha Lite
items.description: S1 E5 | Misty Meaner and Mocha Lite have not only been doing drag for over ten years, but they have been dating for just as long. In this episode, explore the on stage and behind the scenes life of Brooklyn's longest lasting and most loved drag couple.

items.title: Charlene
items.description: S1 E6 | Charlene is a Brooklyn legend on an intimate journey through drag. This episode explores Charlene as she finds freedom in her own skin and is able to celebrate her evolving gender identity through drag.

items.title: Thorgy Thor
items.description: S2 E1 | Thorgy Thor is one of the veteran queens of the Brooklyn drag scene. In addition to being a top 6 finalist in RuPaul's Drag Race Season 8, Thorgy Thor has captured the hearts and respect of her peers and fans alike. Behind the makeup, Thorgy is a trained cellist, and in this episode, in addition to giving her perspective on the scene she has long called home, Thorgy expresses her long held desire to merge her love of drag and classical music.

items.title: Amber Alert
items.description: S2 E2 | Amber may not look like your typical drag queen when painted up, but her performance and charisma speak for themselves. Amber's engaging performance and her descriptions of gender fluidity and how it has affected her life provide for not only an entertaining but inspiring and informational experience.

items.title: Biblegirl
items.description: S2 E3 | Biblegirl represents a new type of drag queen for a new generation. In addition to her stunning performances, Biblegirl is known as a social media queen and has garnered a reputation of being rough around the edges, especially when dealing with her online haters. In this episode, Biblegirl explores her embrace of the online community and how she thinks it has expanded the way drag performers can interact with their fans and build it into a brand.

items.title: Aja
items.description: S2 E4 | Aja has burst onto the Brooklyn drag scene and left her mark. Originally from Bushwick before it was hip, Aja has, throughout her career, bridged the gap between the outer boroughs and introduced a new sense of vitality to a vibrant scene. Through her unique looks and her much-applauded styling and sewing skills, Aja has earned the respect of her peers and uses such praise to inspire her audience.

items.title: Patti Spliff
items.description: S2 E5 | Patti Spliff is a stunning art drag queen who has captivated the Brooklyn scene. Follow Patti as she leaves her Brooklyn surroundings to perform in Fire Island Pines, a common summer stomping ground for the New York gay community. While the queens may be out of the city, the high heels remain on the beach.

items.title: Charlene
items.description: S2 E6 | Charlene, also featured in season 1 of Queens of Kings, has changed since her last appearance. Since Season 1, Charlene has begun the medical process of transitioning from male to female. This episode examines the progress of Charlene's transitions and also explores the effect these changes have made on her mental health and view of the world and her fellow performers.

items.title: Bushwig
items.description: S2 E7 | Bushwig is Brooklyn's largest drag festival, and was created by veteran drag performer Horrorchata. Focusing on Bushwig 2015, the festival featured performances from the cast of Queens of Kings as well as Lady Bunny, Horrorchata, and other Brooklyn drag legends.

items.title: Aquaria
items.description: S3 E1 | Aquaria has had a whirlwind of a year. As the newly crowned winner of Season 10 of RuPaul's Drag Race, she has gone from a New York City icon to an international drag superstar. Aquaria's legendary makeup skills, awe-inspiring looks, and dedication to the craft prove why the Age of Aquaria is upon us.

items.title: Miz Jade
items.description: S3 E2 | Miz Jade, or the Queen of Shade, as she's known to her friends, is a legend of the Brooklyn drag community. While she's a talented dancer and budding seamstress, Miz Jade is known for slaying looks, her kind-spirit, and her avante-garde performances.

items.title: Scarlet Envy
items.description: S3 E3 | Scarlet Envy has been a mainstay of the Brooklyn drag community for years. Now this sultry songstress is trying something new with the debut of her drag cabaret, Smoke and Mirrors. Scarlet's breathtaking looks and captivating talent will have you red with envy.

items.title: Emi Grate
items.description: S4 E1 | QUEENS OF KINGS celebrates the eclectic personalities and diversity of the Brooklyn drag scene. This episode focuses on EMI GRATE, a Burmese refugee powerhouse who is using their drag to help spread a positive world message. Through their eccentric live performances, their powerful digital performances, or their day job in the medical community, EMI GRATE uses their platform to spread a positive message of peace, love, and drag.

items.title: Novaczar
items.description: S4 E2 | QUEENS OF KINGS celebrates the eclectic personalities and diversity of the Brooklyn drag scene. NOVACZAR is a musical powerhouse who recently competed on a global singing competition. This episode will showcase NOVACZAR’s journey to continue to build their musical career, with some help from their drag mother HONEY DAVENPORT, and navigate the complex world of life after reality television.

items.title: The Cake Boys
items.description: S4 E3 | QUEENS OF KINGS celebrates the eclectic personalities and diversity of the Brooklyn drag scene. THE CAKE BOYS are a renowned drag king & things troupe that are making their impact in the Brooklyn nightlife scene. This episode features the empowering tale of SWEATY EDDIE, RICHARD, MUSCLES MONTY and SENERIO as they work together to create a broader platform for drag kings, non-binary performers and everything in between within in a world filled with drag queens.

items.title: Junior Mintt
items.description: S4 E4 | QUEENS OF KINGS celebrates the eclectic personalities and diversity of the Brooklyn drag scene. In this episode, JUNIOR MINTT speaks her truth and calls out the system that was built to suppress queer and trans voices. A prominent NYC trans activist and founder of an ever-expanding inclusive make-up line, JUNIOR MINTT uses her platform to spread a message of inclusivity and acceptance of the black trans community.

items.title: Rify Royalty
items.description: S4 E5 | QUEENS OF KINGS celebrates the eclectic personalities of the Brooklyn drag scene. In this episode, discover the gender norm breaking NYC nightlife fixture RIFY ROYALTY. While they may not seem like your typical drag queen, with their muscles, mustache and Middle Eastern background, RIFY ROYALTY has carved a niche in the Brooklyn drag community by hosting one of the longest running gender-bending parties, Straight Acting, and being a consistently polished, professional and sultry diva.

items.title: The Dragon Sisters
items.description: S4 E6 | QUEENS OF KINGS celebrates the eclectic personalities and diversity of the Brooklyn drag scene. THE DRAGON SISTERS are taking the NYC nightlife and fashion scenes by storm and not looking back. As their profile rises, the powerhouse duo are showcasing their musical skills and looking damn fine while doing it. In this episode, ISSA DRAGON and ODESSA DRAGON pull back the curtain on THE DRAGON SISTERS and give viewers a peek inside their fantastic over the top lives.

items.title: Julie J
items.description: S5 E1 | Julie J is described as an “icon” of the Brooklyn drag community; this word, however, doesn’t do enough to encompass all the work and artistry Julie J has brought to the scene in her short time in NYC. Julie J uses her performances and platform to affect real change in the community, all while turning jaw-dropping looks. Her fundraising events have raised hundreds of thousands of dollars for underserved communities throughout the country, and she’s just getting started!

items.title: God Complex
items.description: S5 E2 | God Complex is an enigma in the Brooklyn drag community. They are a multi-hyphenate who’s art transcends belief and their mind-blowing movement-based performances astound and amaze audiences. In their episode of QUEENS OF KINGS, find out what inspires and drives God Complex in their various dance and drag performances, whether they’re on stage or directing from behind the scenes.

items.title: David Puck
items.description: S5 E3 | In the vast Brooklyn drag community, David Puck isn’t just a storyteller, he’s the storybook! His unique drag styling, penchant for dressing up as inanimate objects, and improv-style performances are a breath of fresh air on the scene. In addition to being a season drag performer, David Puck is also a talented and accomplished muralist. In his QUEENS OF KINGS episode, explore not only David Puck the storyteller, but also David Puck the artist.

items.title: Show Ponii
items.description: S5 E4 | In his QUEENS OF KINGS episode, Show Ponii is self-described as a “trans masc ingenue.” This badass Brooklyn drag king, far from innocent, is taking the world by storm and holding no prisoners along the way. His distinct drag style and rock star performances are only part of the reason this award winning king is so in demand. Surrounding himself with a strong friend group, a drag performing partner and the support of the queer community, Show Ponii is truly unstoppable.

items.title: Honey Davenport
items.description: S5 E5 | Honey Davenport has traveled the world as a singer, dancer, actor, drag superstar, and club DJ. Their career has spanned over 15 years and they have multiple accolades to their name, including 19 pageant crowns and a stint on the most famous drag competition show on television. In their QUEENS OF KINGS episode, take a look behind the scenes and find out what keeps them going, what influences their music and performance style, and what makes Honey Davenport the legend they are!

items.title: Chiquitita
items.description: S5 E6 | Chiquitita is a phenom in the Brooklyn community who uses the stage to amplify queer performance and trans voices. Since a young age, Chiquitita has made her presence known and her impact forceful. Whether on screen, on stage, or in the community, Chiquitita makes sure her voice is the loudest and most powerful with her empowering opinions on a variety of topics that empower her fellow trans, queer and underrepresented sisters.

items.title: Savannah
items.description: S1 E1 | A ray of light in the LGBTQ+ youth community, Savannah aspires to be a Disney animator one day. She is a member of the Mormon church and has been all of her life, however when Savannah came out to her to ward during a sacrament meeting a year ago, the Bishop had her microphone turned off, stopping her right before she had wrapped up her speech. She has since become an advocate for LGBTQ+ teens.

items.title: Cody
items.description: S1 E2 | Cody (Elton Cray) is a professional musician & rapper. We did an initial interview with him in his home, then visited with him almost 10 months later at one of his shows. An interesting and passionate man who speaks his mind, Cody's music is about his struggles with himself and others around him who have been indifferent to how he identifies.

items.title: Miles
items.description: S1 E3 | Miles and Matthias have an adorable father/son relationship. They’ve seen some hard times, but it’s brought them closer together. Miles talks about what it was like for him to go through a divorce as an LGBTQ+ teenager.

items.title: Zach
items.description: S1 E4 | Zach is a track runner and college-bound gay teenager living in Pasadena, California.  Once he became more aware of feelings he was having towards other boys, he started running track.  It  was  a  way  for  him to  keep  his  body  and  mind  occupied  while  he  worked  through  how  to  deal  with  being  "different." His efforts on the field and in the classroom have gotten him noticed by some top-notch Ivy League colleges.

items.title: Eden
items.description: S1 E5 | We interviewed  Eden  and  Stacey  at home  and  at  their  Synagogue. Eden gave us an informative interview on how ze lives life as a gender non-binary teenager.  It was cute to zer ’s mom still struggling with the pronouns, though trying so hard, she respects in every way how Eden identifies and supports zer fully. Stacey and Eden talked to us about being LGBTQ+ in Judaism as well.

items.title: Tyler
items.description: S1 E6 | Tyler is sweet, fierce, and confident. Tyler came out to us on camera as TRANS during one of our interviews with him. He had incredible words of wisdom for President Trump and some vulnerable stories about how tough it is for trans boys in school.

items.title: The Joy of Solo Sex
items.description: S1 E1 | Dana delivers a big package. Sterling receives some very, very scary news.

items.title: The Battery Life of a Hitachi
items.description: S1 E2 | Sterling is very, very sad and drunk; Billie does a Drew Barrymore impression. They come up with a plan!

items.title: Swap! In the Name of Love
items.description: S1 E3 | It's Billie's straight brother Dom's birthday!

items.title: Years & Years of Sex in the Missionary Position
items.description: S1 E4 | It's time for the first real test! Billie and Sterling meet Ms. Hutchcroft, the immigration official.

items.title: Tinder Haikus
items.description: S1 E5 | Billie goes to work at the comedy club.

items.title: Tom Cruise is Aging into Tig Notaro
items.description: S1 E6 | Sterling and Billie keep up the super, super good work of passing as straight at the local gym. Dana makes another delivery.

items.title: Lea Delaria's Strap-On
items.description: S1:E7 | Ms. Hutchcroft makes a home visit.

items.title: The Last Customer of the Night
items.description: S1 E8 | Billie and Sterling come to a tough realization.

items.title: The Walk-In Closet: Inside the Walk-In Closet
items.description: Extras | The performers of The Walk-In Closet chat about representation, playing straight, and going to "queer camp!"

items.title: The Walk-In Closet: Outtakes
items.description: Extras | All the goodies that didn't make it into the episodes!

items.title: Love
items.description: S1 E1 | We hear a lot from the haters, but what about the lovers? Trans people of color explore intimacy with those they hold dear.

items.title: Family
items.description: S1 E2 | When it comes to family, it’s complicated. Join trans people of color who heal from trauma, stay proud of where we came from, and build a future with loved ones.

items.title: Advocacy
items.description: S1 E3 | Living is an act of resistance in a society that denies your existence. From striving for visibility to responding to being outed, trans people of color learn to fight back. #WeWontBeErased

items.title: It's Complicated
items.description: S1 E1 | Meet On Mekahel, model and entrepreneur, as he starts the M.O. Underwear brand with ex-boyfriend Mateusz, days after their breakup. Trouble strikes as On plans a business trip to the factory in LA on Mateusz' birthday weekend.

items.title: Stitches
items.description: S1 E2 | On and Mateusz' trip to the factory in LA proves stressful in the wake of last-minute alterations and repairs to the samples as the day of the photoshoot draws near.

items.title: Full Disclosure
items.description: S1 E3 | Trouble strikes for On during a visit to the PR firm.

items.title: Sources
items.description: S1 E4 | After an intense trip in LA, On travels to his home country of Israel to promote the brand. Things sour after On hears talk of Mateusz' plans for the future.

items.title: Preparation
items.description: S1 E5 | On’s having a hard time with his producers and last minute changes on the eve of the big photoshoot.

items.title: Close-Up
items.description: S1 E6 | In the season finale of Putting On, M.O. Underwear faces the big photoshoot.

items.title: Glam vs. Reality
items.description: S2 E1 | While On is working on his new MO underwear collection and traveling to Los Angeles to do press for his show, his fiancé struggles to navigate a broken justice system in an effort to find out more details about the end of his parole program since On’s dreams of a perfect wedding depend on it.

items.title: Everyone Dreams
items.description: S2 E2 | On meets with his perfume factory before traveling to Tel Aviv for a photoshoot and clothing line collaboration. Meanwhile, we get to know a bit more about his fiancée and his connection to personal training. On is encouraging Dave to open his own gym and dream big.

items.title: I Love You NYC
items.description: S2 E3 | As their time in NYC comes to a close, On dives deeper into his work while trying to close last minute details on a wedding ceremony in Paris. The couple find time to do one last food run, muckbanging their favorite food spots around the city.

items.title: We Will Always Have Paris
items.description: S2 E4 | On and Dave take a break between life in New York and their new beginning in Los Angeles as they travel to Israel for some reflection. Later on they head to Paris, the city of love, for an intimate wedding ceremony.

items.title: California Dreaming
items.description: S2 E5 | As soon as it seems they begin to vibe California dream life, things take a turn. On begins hosting a weekly web cast as Dave is laid off. Fear about the future in Los Angeles looms but On tries to stay optimistic.

items.title: Baby Goat Baby
items.description: S2 E6 | In the final episode of the season, On’s brand continues to evolve as new partnerships are considered. Dave surprises On with a field trip and the couple seriously discuss moving home to New York City.

items.title: The Confessional
items.description: S2 E7 | Go behind the scenes with these confessionals from season two of Putting On!

items.title: Where are My Friiieeends
items.description: S1 E1 | Adrian’s event doesn’t go as expected. Leacy prepares a first date. Sethe unveils his new art installation and it leaves D’ante with questions. Casey’s hook up isn’t quite what he expected and Blaine has problems adjusting.

items.title: #ClassicCasey
items.description: S1 E2 | S*@% goes down with Casey and the group is left trying to pick up the pieces.

items.title: BLOWN by Bocaj

items.title: Pilot
items.description: S1 E1 | Kieran Davis recently lost his job at a record label and decides to freelance as a manager. He gets approached on the street by Aaron Hunter, a cocky hip hop artist selling CDs on the street. After Aaron raps a few bars, Kieran offers to take him on as his new client. They forge a friendship as business partners. Through Kieran’s connections, Aaron reaches mild success by getting his song played on the radio and a record deal with Maximum records. The success is short lived and all comes crashing down when Maxine, the owner of the record label rests the future of their careers on Aaron's next song.

items.title: The Kiss
items.description: S1 E2 | Aaron’s apartment gets broken into and all of his original music is stolen. DJ Bizzy, Aaron’s producer sets him up with a boy band frontman turned solo artist, Harmon Vegas to cowrite a new song. Aaron feels Harmon is the reason why the record label isn’t pushing his career as strong as they should. Back at home, Kieran learns his girlfriend is pregnant. While in the studio, Bizzy and Kieran leave Aaron and Harmon alone so their creative juices can flow. After a few drinks they share intimate details about their lives and discover they are more similar than they thought. Harmon moves in for a kiss that changes their lives forever.

items.title: Young Lovers
items.description: S1 E3 | Taken back by what transpired in the studio, Aaron stops talking to Harmon until Bizzy gets them back together. Harmon questions Aaron's fear and encourages him to embrace his truth. Kieran grows skeptical of Harmon's motives and learns the record label plans to drop Aaron and focus more on Harmon's career. Shai gets his own apartment and starts planning a comeback. Suffering from financial woes, Kieran makes a deal with a drug dealer to support his incoming family and keep Aaron’s career afloat. Harmon gets Aaron to let go of his fears, they share an intimate moment that allows Aaron to open up and co-write his first sincere song, Young Lovers.

items.title: I Never Want to See You Again
items.description: S1 E4 | Aaron admits he is dating Harmon by coming out to Shai whose response is not the good news he hoped for. Fearful of more rejection, Aaron goes on a radio show and lies about working with Harmon by taking full credit for writing his new song and claims he is dating his ex-girlfriend, Reesa Evans. Sheila, Kieran’s girlfriend gets into an argument with Kieran after flirting with the idea of an abortion. Shai’s drug dealer learns a secret about Shai and severs all ties with him. Kieran flips out on Aaron for lying on the radio show and tells Aaron that he is getting dropped from the label.

items.title: A Call for Help
items.description: S1 E5 | After hearing Aaron lie on radio show, Harmon breaks up with him. Shai takes Aaron’s stolen music and passes it off as his own. Bizzy is desperate for money and takes Shai on as a client. Reesa confronts Aaron and learns that he was dropped from his record label. Maxine signs Shai as her new artist and debuts his song on a radio show. Harmon tries to cover up his fall out with Aaron publicly. Kieran and Bizzy try to find peace in all of the chaos until a phone call changes their lives.

items.title: Finale
items.description: S1 E6 | Reesa reaches out to Harmon and admits that she knows the truth about their relationship. Aaron wakes up in his home with Kieran watching over him and learns that he blacked out. Kieran admits he already knew about his secret relationship. Bizzy learns that Shai’s music was plagiarized and promises to sue. Sheila admits she couldn’t go through with the abortion and that she knew about the drug deal Kieran made. Desperate and confused, Shai finds a gun and invites both Aaron and Kieran over to his house. Aaron and Kieran arrive to reconcile with Shai but are unaware of his true motives.

items.title: Right In My Face
items.description: Right In My Face is a song about discovering yourself after a sudden and unforeseen breakup even though the red flags were right in your face. It is about healing and realizing that despite the heartbreak, everything will be okay. The video uses the concept of the title to portray a post-apocalyptic world where a man who represents innocence is turned to the dark more seductive part of this new future. His inevitable change was right in his face throughout the events of the video.

items.title: Somewhere In Miami
items.description: Picturesque blue skies, pretty girls, and bold colors, “Somewhere in Miami” encompasses the culture, the attitude, and grit Miami has to offer. Chelzzz knows she might not be the most well behaved, but she stays on top of her game, so no one steps over her. She left behind her old life and “manners” in exchange for the highest-end apparel and Rolls Royce flex through the town. Unlike many hip-hop videos where women are sexual commodities and show off because of their seductive appeal, “Somewhere In Miami” portrays women as power figures, where they make the decisions and are the “ballers.” Chelzzz not only works hard and plays hard for herself but makes sure her music is a platform to lift others up as well.

items.title: Loot (feat. Londynn B.)
items.description: What’s better than one diva, but two: Gabby’s newest single “Loot” also features guest vocals by Atlanta rapper Londynn B. A finalist on Netflix’s Rhythm and Flow, Londynn B. is a visionary rapper only on the rise, with an album, collabs, and touring planned for 2020. Gabby B. and Londynn B. make a natural pair both in the track and onscreen. Who needs modesty when you’ve achieved so much? She makes all the things she sings about (high-end brands and endless cash flow) into tangible proclamations; she is showered with bills, rides in private jets and Ferraris, and is decked out in “icy” jewelry.

items.title: Klassy
items.description: Rayner makes his presence felt in the "KLASSY” video as the excitable, enthusiastic, music producer while presenting Jonté in this new incarnation. Jack delivers the song’s hook and he makes it clear that he admires Jonté as much as the audience does during the song verses that all lead to a high paced dance climax. Director Miles Victor Zantos's camera captures a transformation in action: Jonté begins the clip in the midst of a harried day, but after the application of cosmetics and the recovery of his self-possession, he's soon radiant, confident, and ready for the dance floor. When he gets there, he demonstrates why he's been an in-demand choreographer for nearly twenty years. His moves are poised. His outfits are outrageous! It’s sexy, provocative, and absolutely dripping with class.

items.title: Nwaye
items.description: In creole, the word "Nwaye" implies drowning, and the song's narrator is overwhelmed by the deceit and misdirection of the authorities. But everything about Beauvoir's performance is steely, determined, and ultimately, hopeful. Malou Beauvoir sings like someone who has righteousness on her side – and maybe the Vodou spirits, too. Her characteristic amalgam of North American soul, Caribbean sweetness, Haitian traditional music, and international pop has never been more seamlessly integrated as it is here, and it's all put to the service of a very good cause. The clip features dancer and choreographer Raphaëlle François, whose portfolio ranges from performances and workshops in prestigious institutions such as Tokyo National Ballet, Quartier in Paris, Carnegie Hall in New York, the Ballet Hispanico in New York, the Ballet Roto in Dominican Republic, in Cyprus, Jamaica and much more, where she promotes Haitian culture. Those who've followed Malou Beauvoir know that she always cuts an impressive figure in her videos. Although there's also plenty of footage of Haitian protest movements and the ordinary acts of kindness and resistance in the "Nwaye" clip, the star is the focus. At the beginning of the video, the lightning flashes, and the dark clouds threaten to overwhelm the Haitian plain. But by the end, Beauvoir stands, boldly, by a waterfall. She doesn't deny the power of natural forces. Scary though they are, she trusts that they'll sustain her – and her causes, too.

items.title: Waking Up Down
items.description: "Waking Up Down," the lead single off What We Drew, was DIY from front to back, as usual for the self-taught producer and initially reluctant singer. Her soft, whisper-sung vocals began as a cover for her inexperience, but now, they've become a major part of her singular style. It's a spacy breeze of bedroom pop and underground club music, with English and Korean lyrics about the challenges, small victories, and simple euphoria of mastering young adulthood. There's a genuine swagger in her lyrics and her delivery, but it's a confidence that holds out a hand, saying, together, we've got this. While it's built for a packed, illegal dance party, "Waking Up Down" still has the warmth and intimacy of a track that's perfect for zoning out, getting lost in yourself, and liking what you find.

items.title: Boy Kiss
items.description: This song was about trying to find yourself in this world and not being ashamed of what you discover and within that process finding a soulmate and that dream not coming true fully until you’ve completely fallen in love with yourself first. But both are within our grasp. As a queer artist that dives in and take a lot of inspiration through my life experiences as well as dreams into my music, I would be untrue to myself and my craft if I didn’t constantly make reference to my sexuality and lifestyle. When I was little, I would always stare up at the movies and wish someone like me was represented in them. That I wasn’t either comic relief or my life terribly sad and tragic. That I and the one I loved were front and center, shining bright and lived happily ever after. Happily ever after does exist for all of the queer community, in our movie. And we deserve every ounce of it. This project brought together so many talented and amazing people, mostly queer, that shows how much beauty we can put into this world.

Portland isn’t afraid to remind us all that kink is political AF! From Strippers fighting for equal rights and pay amidst a pandemic to Foodie Activism for Sex Workers, Young connects with fellow sexual revolutionaries making a difference in their city. Madison’s explorations lead them to an amazing cast of characters including Nikeisah C. Newton, a chef turned sex worker activist, Cat Hollis - a stripper rights activist and organizer for the Portland Stripper’s Strike, Arabelle Raphael - sex worker and fetishist, and the donut daddy of our dreams, Dadi Iris, who shows us just what those donut holes are really for!

After a laughter-filled afternoon with Young’s friends Dahlia Snow and Nyxie Likley spent exploring the intimate kink of blood play, Young takes a trip down memory lane visiting the site of their former site of the unionized and worker owned peep show - The Lusty Lady - followed by a powerful needle pull ritual with BDSM educator and ritualist - Cleo Dubois.

items.title: Satan's Tears
items.description: Singer songwriter Kyler O’Neal’s debut single “Satan’s Tears” is firstly a love letter to herself and then to everyone else that has felt rejected or outcasted by society. For the video, Kyler’s sense of empathy and her desire that we all hold a complex view of humanity guided the spirit of the endeavor and collaboration. The music video explores mysticism not necessarily as the subject of the video, but where the video itself is the spirit or experience of the mystical. The project was shot in the hills surrounding San Francisco in order to root the performance in the Bay’s rich history as the birthplace of Isadora Duncan - and with her, much of modern dance - and the rise of queer and feminist consciousness and civil rights movements. Choreography was created with Isabelle Sjasham, who in the 2000s ran an underground queer/trans ballet company in the Bay Area and more recently choreographed videos for queer artists such as a Crook. Jewelry and costume design was provided by Stacey Ellen Rich, known for her work on Ron Athey’s opera “Gifts of the Spirit.” The project was the brain-child of gender queer artist and producer Luka Fisher, who met Kyler in a bathroom on the set of director Lyle Kash’s majority trans cast/crew feature, “Death and Bowling.” Other influences were Kate Bush, Maya Deren, Sailor Moon, and early Whitney Houston music videos.
